label: c4-tuned-s0
resisted: The game-theoretic content of the label. The network is a static positional-value map (weighted piece count) plus four one- or two-square corrections; it does not represent threats, odd/even-row parity, zugzwang or open two-in-a-rows. In the 765 training positions where o already has three in a line with the fourth square empty, x wins 26% but the network predicts 49% on average; open twos are the strongest residual signal (r = 0.13). The four non-linear units resisted domain reading: each is a hinge on one or two squares that breaks the symmetric x/o coding of that square (restore gain in total +0.0004 AUC), and none matches a Connect-4 concept; f6_top_square is a large weight fitted to 16 rare positions (x on top of a full column f).
tool_bugs: None blocking. (1) A leaf entry must be inside the leaf's subgraph, so a hidden node read by two leaves (611 -> output and 611 -> 5461) needed split_node; the edge between the two leaves (1722 -> 611_b) then counted as uncovered until a composition (e4_f3_with_f6) listed it in its subgraph_connections. (2) linearise_annotations was called with the 5 leaf names explicitly (known DAG bug with compositions in scope); it ran fine that way. (3) Worktree sandbox refuses compound shell commands with uv; calls went through scratch wrappers call.py / batch.py / run_spec.py. (4) compute_shap with max_samples 1500 on 42 inputs took about 15+ minutes at ~470% CPU.
summary: P(x wins) = sigmoid(-1.78 + board_weighting + four small single-square corrections). board_weighting is a linear map over 29 squares in which a piece is worth most to its owner on low central squares (peak d3, then c3, d2, d4, e3) and slightly negative on the edge columns a and g and on rare top squares; it tracks the classic count of winning lines through each square (r = 0.88) and the network's logit correlates 0.91 with line-count-weighted material. Making every hidden unit linear changes train AUC only from 0.8559 to 0.8555, matching logistic regression (0.857): the network is effectively linear and misses threats and parity, which gradient boosting (0.947) exploits.

leaf_assessments.name: board_weighting
leaf_assessments.hypothesis_short: Linear positional-value map: a piece counts for its owner by how many four-in-a-row lines pass through its square (low centre high, edges and top low).
leaf_assessments.why: Per-square effects correlate 0.88 (x) / 0.86 (o) with the winning-line counts over the 32 commonly occupied squares, peak at d3 as the line counts do (13 lines), and the leaf correlates 0.88 with line-count-weighted material (AUC 0.82 alone). Mean ablation drops AUC 0.856 -> 0.493. Exceptions stated: rows 4+ weighted below rows 2-3, rare top squares get large negative owner weights, and it is blind to threats/parity (o-threat positions predicted 49% vs 26% observed).

leaf_assessments.name: f1_asymmetry
leaf_assessments.hypothesis_short: Hinge on f1: x on f1 +0.46 logit vs empty, o on f1 only -0.12 (o penalty cut off).
leaf_assessments.why: Largest non-linear gain in the network but tiny (restore gain +0.0005 AUC). The asymmetry moves toward a data-fitted one-hot regression (+0.21 for x and for o) but no domain concept (lines through f1 = 4, threats, parity) predicts it; it is a recoding of one square.

leaf_assessments.name: c5_negligible
leaf_assessments.hypothesis_short: Negligible hinge on c5 (x +0.075, o -0.019 logit).
leaf_assessments.why: Support-level near-null: mean ablation changes AUC by 1e-5 and p by <= 0.018; restore gain -0.00002; sign for x disagrees with the one-hot regression.

leaf_assessments.name: e4_f3_pair
leaf_assessments.hypothesis_short: Two squares of the positional map (e4, 11 lines; f3, 8 lines) routed through a hinge that caps the o penalty.
leaf_assessments.why: The per-square values fit the domain and agree with the one-hot regression (e4 +1.37/-0.83 vs +1.20/-0.83; f3 +0.92/-0.83 vs +0.50/-0.65); mean ablation AUC 0.848. The non-linear part (capped o penalty, joint 'diagonal' reading) has no support: 18 positions have both squares occupied and linearising it raises AUC (restore gain -0.00018).

leaf_assessments.name: f6_top_square
leaf_assessments.hypothesis_short: x on f6 (top of a full column f, 16 positions) gives -3.3 logit; otherwise a near-linear rescale of the e4/f3 signal.
leaf_assessments.why: Direction matches the 16 positions (win 0.31, predicted 0.22) but it is a fit to rare positions; stacking three x in column f without x on top (420 positions) has win rate 0.72, so it is not 'wasted pieces in a column'. Restore gain +0.00006.

composition_notes: position_value (root, ann_50): children add in logit with output weights 1.0 (board_weighting), 0.303 (f1), 0.047 (c5), and the composition e4_f3_with_f6 (ann_49) whose two exits are weighted 1.305 (611_a) and -0.095 (5461); 8 unconnected squares (a5, a6, c6, d6, e5, e6, f5, g4) are zero-effect entries of the root. e4_f3_with_f6 is serial (1722 -> 611_b -> 5461) but additive in practice because 611 is always on and 5461 is off in only 59 positions; the f6 path rescales the e4/f3 signal by -0.032.

ground_truth_comparisons.note: Playable (immediately winnable) threats never occur in this dataset (positions with a forced next move are excluded); three-with-empty threats are rare (x 1.2%, o 1.4% of positions).

restore_gain.note: linearise_annotations, train split, 54,045 rows, leaf names passed explicitly. Local check replacing every relu by identity (not best fit): AUC 0.8545.

unit_activity_summary: 611 always on (pure linear relay, split into 611_a/611_b); 5461 on in 53,986 of 54,045 (off only with o on f6); 7084 on in 98% (off with o on c5); 1722 on in 93% (off with o on e4 or f3); 6646 on in 72% (off with o on f1). Every unit depends on one or two squares, so each is a re-coding of those squares' three states.
